name: Ray Kurzweil

summary.text: Ray Kurzweil is an inventor and author who received the 1999 National Medal of Technology for work in computer science including voice recognition. He co-founded Singularity University with Peter Diamandis in 2008; it launched publicly in February 2009 at NASA's Ames research campus with backing from Google and NASA. In December 2012 Google hired him as a director of engineering working on machine learning and language processing. His books The Singularity Is Near (2005) and The Singularity Is Nearer (2024) predict human-level AI by 2029 and a merger of people with machines by 2045, and he has said that from 2029 medical progress will add more than a year of life expectancy per year.

facts.claim: Kurzweil is listed by the USPTO among the five laureates of the 1999 National Medal of Technology, awarded by President Bill Clinton; his citation credits achievements in computer science such as voice recognition.
facts.quote: His citation credits pioneering and innovative achievements in computer science such as voice recognition.

sources.title: 1999 Laureates - National Medal of Technology and Innovation

facts.claim: Singularity University was co-founded in 2008 by Peter Diamandis and Kurzweil and launched publicly on February 2-3, 2009 at NASA's Ames research campus in California, announced at the TED conference with backing from Google and NASA. It is not an accredited university; it sells executive education and runs programs on exponential technologies.
facts.quote: Kurzweil and Diamandis will unveil plans for the new university today at the annual TED (Technology, Entertainment and Design) Conference in Long Beach, California.

facts.claim: In December 2012 Google hired Kurzweil as a director of engineering. He said in an email that it was a full-time position in Mountain View focused on machine learning and language processing, and that he would keep his public speaking and writing role. His Singularity University biography describes him as heading a Google team developing machine intelligence and natural language understanding.
facts.quote: He announced that he had been hired by Google as a director of engineering focused on machine learning and language processing.

sources.title: Ray Kurzweil Joins Google In Full-Time Engineering Director Role; Will Focus On Machine Learning, Language Processing

facts.claim: Kurzweil has said that medical science currently adds about four months of longevity per year and that by 2029 it will add a full year, a threshold he calls longevity escape velocity. In a Bessemer Venture Partners interview he said: 'After 2029, you'll gain more than a year back. You'll go backward in time.' He attributes this to simulating biology on computers and AI-driven drug design.
facts.quote: After 2029, you'll gain more than a year back. You'll go backward in time.

facts.claim: The Singularity Summit, an annual conference on AI, brain-computer interfaces, robotics and regenerative medicine, was founded in 2006 by the Singularity Institute (now MIRI), Kurzweil and Peter Thiel; the first was held at Stanford University. In December 2012 Singularity University acquired the Summit from the Singularity Institute.
facts.quote: The conference was founded by MIRI, Ray Kurzweil, and Peter Thiel in 2006.

openQuestions: Whether Kurzweil still holds the Google post in 2026 was not checked.
The 2024 book's 2029 and 2045 dates were only seen in Wikipedia-derived text; a review or publisher page should be cited before they are used as a fact.
Kurzweil's reported revision of the longevity timeline to 2029-2035 in The Economist (2024) came from a blog and was left out.
The Bessemer interview quote is reported through Popular Mechanics; the original interview was not opened.
